My Time
to Recharge

After work and university, I need simple moments to slow down. Music, a short walk, a movie, or a quiet break at home help me feel better without requiring a lot of time or money.

My starting point

This is my daily context

I work from 7:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. as a junior software developer, and I also study online. Because my weekdays are busy, I do not wait for a completely free day. I use short moments in the evening and more time on weekends.

Economic context

Simple and affordable

I choose activities that fit my budget. Walking, listening to music, and watching something at home cost little or nothing.

Social context

Time with other people

Talking with my family or friends helps me disconnect from screens and feel connected to them.

Cultural context

Music and stories

I enjoy music and movies in Spanish. I can also watch short videos in English to practice the language.

Personal context

Technology with limits

I like learning about technology, but I also need moments away from the computer because I use it for work and study.

Questions from the activity

Free time and relaxation

These answers describe what I actually do and how I try to balance my responsibilities with rest.

01

How can using free time wisely improve your physical and mental health?

Using my free time well can help me recover from a long day. When I walk for a few minutes or stretch at home, my body feels less tense. When I listen to music, I stop thinking about pending tasks for a moment.

I know that I cannot do everything every day. For that reason, I prefer short activities that fit my schedule. I should also sleep enough and take breaks from the screen.

Grammar in context: walk, stretch, listen show actions; know, prefer describe states; can, should express possibility and advice.

02

What is the importance of relaxation activities in your life?

Relaxation is important in my life because I need a pause between work and university. If I continue using the computer without resting, it is harder for me to concentrate. A quiet break can help me start my classes or assignments with a clearer mind.

I like listening to music and watching movies at home. I also enjoy learning about technology, but I must set limits. Resting does not mean ignoring my responsibilities. It helps me continue them in a calmer way.

These ideas connect modal verbs with everyday decisions, as explained by Quinn (2023), and use stative and action verbs in familiar situations (Muñoz-Ortiz, 2020).

What I really enjoy

My free-time choices

I choose these activities because they are realistic for my schedule and my budget. They also show the grammar from the course in natural sentences.

I enjoy listening to music

I often use my earphones when I walk. Music helps me change the rhythm of the day.

I want to learn new tools

This is my real study space. I enjoy practicing technology at my own pace.

I like taking quiet breaks

A calm place helps me pause and enjoy a moment away from the computer.

I like spending time with other people

Talking and sharing simple moments outdoors are part of my social well-being.

Connection with Week 2 enjoy listening, like taking, and like spending use gerunds. want to learn uses an infinitive. The teacher's Week 2 material helped me review these patterns before using action, stative, and modal verbs in this mural.
Second guiding question

How do I organize my free time?

I do not follow this plan perfectly every day. It is a simple guide that helps me avoid leaving all my university work or all my rest for the weekend.

3:30 p.m.

End of my workday

I take a short pause and have something to eat before starting university activities.

Early evening

University first

I check deadlines and complete the most urgent activity. A short list helps me focus.

Later at night

One simple hobby

I listen to music or watch part of a movie. I do not need a long activity to enjoy my free time.

Weekend

More flexible time

I can walk, finish a movie, talk with my family, or explore a technology topic that interests me.

Small decisions

What self-care means to me

For me, self-care is practical. It means noticing when I am tired and making a small adjustment instead of continuing automatically.

My weekly check

I can use this list to notice what I am doing, without expecting a perfect routine.

I should rest.

If I am very tired, a pause may be more useful than forcing myself to continue.

I can move.

A short walk or a stretch is possible even on a busy weekday.

I must set limits.

Work, study, and hobbies all involve screens, so I need moments without one.

I could change the plan.

If I have little time, I can listen to two songs instead of watching a full movie.

Multimedia resource

Action and stative verbs

This short lesson complements the mural and helps distinguish actions from states, thoughts, emotions, and preferences.

Personal reflection

While preparing this mural, I noticed that English grammar appears in ordinary decisions. I use action verbs to explain what I do, stative verbs to describe what I like or need, and modal verbs to talk about options and responsibilities.

I also learned that organizing free time does not require an expensive activity or a perfect schedule. In my case, a short break is more realistic than planning several hours every day.

“A small pause can make the rest of my day easier.”
